summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/8)

data.turoyo: E məd Aloho hawxa kuwele raḏ̣a, u zadano stene kmoṭe, kšoʕəṯ, kowe waxt du ḥṣodo.
data.translation: So Gott will, wird das Getreide reif. Es färbt sich gelb und die Erntezeit rückt heran.

rationale: First Infectum box; unambiguous crop yellowing with maturity and harvest context.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.33/5480)

data.turoyo: Bu ṭarbo kowe, u ṭarbano u grišo d kətyo ʕal ah hnavad (ag gəwoye) du nošo layt, kšoʕəṯ.
data.translation: It is in the spleen; that spleen, the elongated one which is over a person's innards, is absent, it withers.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; explicit organ subject with the inherited withering meaning, retained as a reported folk account without medical inference. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.5/1469)

data.turoyo: <...> daqne ḥəworo, u ḥəworo ste šaʕəṯ. Mu šəʕoṯo ste čiki am mene b feme. Brim u daqnayḏe, yaʕni mede sowo yo. <...>
data.translation: <...> his beard white, and the white was also shaggy. From its shagginess some of it stuck into his mouth. His beard was curled, that is, he was an old man. <...>

rationale: Single attestation establishing restricted new I.2. Explanatory nominal context supports texture rather than colour; capitalization and source spelling retained. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: Crop yellowing and human pallor share inherited sense 1. JTM 1.1/8 supplies a secure Infectum example; no new meaning is needed.
The apple can be yellow before it is ripe at 62/161, while crop yellowing accompanies maturation in JTM 1.1/8. Yellowing must not be glossed as becoming ripe.
JL 6.10/15 remains ko-Preterit, distinct from the unprefixed Preterit Intransitive human-pallor examples. Echo repetition at 69/100 is one state, not a second event.
JTM 2.3/2 has šuḥṯiwo among growing, yellowing and hardening pumpkins. Its context supports the semantic comparison, but spelling alone does not establish this root's Infectum-wa.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.
Jan crop kšuʕṯi supports the Infectum established in round 1; repeated new_form proposals are consolidated without a second box. Yellowing and ripening remain distinct.

The beard clause supplies a distinct texture reading, limited to one source passage and reinforced by the quality noun šəʕoṯo. Its exact nuance is less secure than the contrast with colour; no general grow-hair sense is proposed.
The clothes description (Jan 2.4/927) is not used to widen the new beard sense or the inherited colour sense without a secure contextual reading. It remains an unresolved occurrence decision.
Ṭarbo clauses are evidence for Turoyo participant and aspect usage only; absence/withering in a reported bodily account does not establish the anatomy or diagnosis in the English.
No agent, affected l-suffix or Detransitive alternation is shown. Human pallor, crop yellowing and the organ account use subject-state coding.
Collate šuḥṯiwo in JTM 2.3/2 with the source/audio: is ḥ a realization of ʕ before ṯ, or a transcription error? Confirm the root and Infectum-wa analysis before adding the box.
Do crop yellowing and human pallor have any systematic dialectal or valency distinctions beyond the participant difference? The present evidence does not show one.
At Jan 2.5/1469, does šaʕəṯ of the beard mean straggly, disordered, overlong, or specifically untrimmed? The new sense is deliberately restricted to shaggy texture pending refinement.
Confirm whether šəʕoṯo is an independently lexicalized quality noun or a regular nominal derivative; no Infinitiv box is established from it.
At Jan 2.4/927, do šaʕiṯi clothes have faded colour or damaged/disordered texture? The supplied English ragged cannot settle the Turoyo meaning.
What physical condition is attributed to ṭarbo at Jan 2.33/5479-5480? Preserve the inherited withering gloss without adding a medical sense.
Reported ṭarbo withering extends the affected participant from whole plants/people to an internal organ; no independent technical disease meaning is established.
